title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is a case of political impersonation using generative video. A candidate's likeness and voice were used to produce statements she never made, and the fabricated clips were published on a social platform by her opponent's campaign. The failure sits at the point of publication rather than in any automated decision: a person or campaign chose to post synthetic media depicting a real, identifiable individual saying things she did not say.

Catching this required no model evaluation or red-teaming, because the falsehood was not hidden inside a system's output. It required the platform or the poster to treat a synthetic depiction of a named candidate as something needing disclosure or removal, and it required the target to notice the clips and respond. The cease-and-desist letter is that response, and it asserts defamation exposure under state law while stating that legal options are still being weighed.

What is not established is whether the videos were intended to deceive, whether any defamation claim will be filed or succeed, and whether the platforms hosting them will act. A cease-and-desist letter is a demand, not a ruling, and the campaign's dismissal of it is a statement, not a finding.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI-generated deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden has posted videos to X showing fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including one shared on Aug. 4. The letter, dated Sept. 30, says Cooke never made those statements and accuses Van Orden of trying to fool voters and harm her reputation.

The letter warns that Van Orden could face defamation claims under state law and says Cooke's attorneys are monitoring his accounts and weighing all legal options. Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum. Cooke criticized the videos in a statement. Van Orden responded on social media with another AI-generated video featuring a duck saying "Cease and desist!" Cooke lost to Van Orden by about 3 percentage points in 2024.
